solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Insert provided in posh catalogue (8)

indicators.note: tells you to put one piece inside another
says where the inserted piece goes: inside 'posh'

annotation.surface: An editor tucks a supplement into a glossy upmarket catalogue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Insert' and 'catalogue' both look like nouns from publishing; here 'Insert' is an instruction and 'catalogue' is the verb being defined.
annotation.definitionFit: To catalogue things is to classify them, sorting them into categories.

entries.clue: Heavy metal piano bores manager (6)

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the piano letter goes into the middle of the manager

blocks.note: a coper is one who copes, i.e. manages

annotation.surface: A rock fan complains that the piano parts in heavy metal bore the band's manager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' reads as the music genre, and piano and manager keep you in the band; in fact it is the chemist's category, a dense metallic element.
annotation.definitionFit: Copper is a dense metallic element, so counts as a heavy metal.

entries.clue: Each nest individually overturned antenna (6)

indicators.note: each piece is turned round on its own rather than the whole thing at once

blocks.note: ea. is the standard abbreviation for each, as on a price list
a lair is an animal's den or nest

annotation.surface: Birds have built nests on a rooftop antenna, and each one has been knocked over.
annotation.walkthrough: Reversing EALAIR as one string gives RIALAE, which is useless; 'individually' tells you to flip EA and LAIR separately and keep them in clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: An aerial is the antenna that picks up radio or TV signals.

entries.clue: Friend pursuing tasteless drawing (9)

definitions.note: 'drawing' is a gerund here, the act of ending level; stalemate is the noun for that result.

indicators.note: the friend chases, so comes after, the word for tasteless

annotation.surface: A friend follows someone who has made a crude, tasteless sketch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests a picture; it is the present participle of draw, a game ending level, as a chess stalemate does.
annotation.definitionFit: Stalemate in chess is a way of drawing the game, so it names a drawing of the match.

entries.clue: Misshapen ice? A chef must accept consequences (4,3,5)

indicators.note: the letters that follow are to be bent into a new shape

annotation.surface: A chef, blamed for a lopsided ice sculpture, has to own up.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the surface into a kitchen disaster and its verdict, which hides that 'ice? A chef must' is one run of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To face the music is to accept the unpleasant consequences of what you have done.

entries.clue: Call secretary to return ring (6)

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the secretary's letters come back the other way

blocks.note: a peal is a ring of bells

annotation.surface: A boss asks for the secretary to come back and phone someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Call' and 'ring' both look like phoning; 'Call' is the definition in the sense of a plea, and 'ring' is a peal of bells.
annotation.definitionFit: An appeal is a call, an earnest request for help or support.

entries.clue: Crowd ahead of Spurs on sidelines (5)

indicators.note: the sidelines are a pitch's edges, so take just the edge letters of Spurs

blocks.note: first and last letters of Spurs

annotation.surface: Before a Tottenham Hotspur match, a crowd gathers along the touchlines.
annotation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club, and 'sidelines' fits that picture; here it means the outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A press is a crowd of people pushing together.

entries.clue: Cold stuffing on the way, baked in pastry (2,6)

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside, so cold sits inside 'on the way'

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A cold stuffing is packed into a pie while it travels.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface stays in the kitchen, so 'stuffing' reads as the filling; it is the instruction to insert.
annotation.definitionFit: En croute is the French cookery term for food wrapped and baked in pastry, as in beef Wellington.

entries.clue: Letter turned whimsical, gripping as well (8)

indicators.note: turned round, so whimsical's letters run backwards
the turned word holds another inside it

blocks.note: droll = amusing in an odd, whimsical way

annotation.surface: A written letter has taken an oddly whimsical turn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' reads as something you post; it is one who lets property.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: anyone who lets out property is a letter, and a landlord is the obvious one.

entries.clue: Standard item of cavalier language (8)

blocks.note: par = the standard, as in 'up to par'
a lance is a mounted soldier's weapon

annotation.surface: A dashing horseman's swagger is typical of the way he talks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' in the surface is an adjective meaning offhand; the wordplay needs the noun, a horseman who carries a lance.
annotation.definitionFit: Parlance is a way of speaking, a particular language or idiom.

entries.clue: Signal to turn right? (6)

blocks.note: to turn into something is to become one: to be a...

annotation.surface: A driver's indicator flashes to show they are about to go right.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about indicating at a junction; the wordplay is political: to turn right is to become a Tory, to 'be a Con'.
annotation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light used as a signal.

entries.clue: Jargon on a ship upset North American — one from Harvard? (12)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the next
in a down clue, upset turns the letters upwards, reversing them

blocks.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

annotation.surface: A North American student at Harvard is seasick, fed up with naval jargon.
annotation.walkthrough: Cantabrigian usually means of Cambridge, England; Harvard is in Cambridge, Massachusetts, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Harvard stands in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so its people are, loosely, Cantabrigian.

entries.clue: Heading for escalator, passed on lift (5)

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the late = those who have passed on, died

annotation.surface: Someone walks past the escalator and takes the lift instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lift' sits beside 'escalator' and looks like an elevator; it is the verb, to raise someone's spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'lift' here is the verb for raising someone's spirits, not the elevator.

entries.clue: Before promotions, implement toxic growth (9)

indicators.note: puts 'to' first in the chain

blocks.note: to = before, as in 'ten to six'

annotation.surface: A company warns that its new marketing plan will spread through the business like a poison.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' is doing double work: it gives the letters TO, and it also sets them at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a fungus, often poisonous, so a toxic growth.

entries.clue: Warning to PR team, scrambling behind collapse (6,6)

indicators.note: the PR team's letters are jumbled
the jumbled letters come after the word for collapse

annotation.surface: The press office is scrambling to handle a warning after something went wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Caveat emptor is Latin for 'let the buyer beware', the traditional warning that the purchaser takes the risk.
annotation.definitionFit: Caveat emptor is a warning to buyers that they must check what they buy.

entries.clue: Possibly some faint political statement (9)

indicators.note: the letters that follow are one possible arrangement, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: A party's policy document might be a little limp.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a gibe at a feeble party programme, which keeps 'some faint' looking like ordinary words.
annotation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a party's published political statement of aims.

entries.clue: Hard to go in for length of friendly game (8)

indicators.note: one letter goes in in place of another

annotation.surface: Tough rules have been brought in to limit how long a friendly match lasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friendly game' reads as a sports fixture; 'game' is the definition, birds shot for sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Pheasant is game, a bird hunted for sport and food.

entries.clue: Youngster favoured extremely rascally manipulation (8)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters, of rascally

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog, or a cheeky youngster
first and last letters of rascally

annotation.surface: A favoured child is running a very crafty scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier of 'rascally'; here it takes that word's extreme letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the working of puppets, and figuratively the manipulation of people.

entries.clue: Man contributing to partnership on home ground? (12)

definitions.text: Man contributing to partnership on home ground?

blocks.note: the surface suggests a business or sporting partner; the partnership is a marriage
sounds like a match at the home stadium; it means his contribution is made in the house

annotation.surface: A footballer playing for his side at their own stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partnership' and 'home ground' suggest sport; the partnership is a marriage and the home ground is the house.
annotation.definitionFit: A househusband is a married man who keeps house, contributing at home to the marriage.

entries.clue: Delivered cheeses for picnic (6)

indicators.note: delivered as a speech is, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

annotation.surface: Soft cheeses have been brought round for an outdoor lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' belongs with the cheeses in the surface; it is the informal sense, something easy, as in 'no picnic'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'no picnic' means hard work, so a picnic is anything easy, and the answer is the same informal sense.

entries.clue: Wine selection from customer lottery (6)

indicators.note: a run of letters is picked out of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A customer wins a choice of wine in a raffle.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words, which the raffle picture keeps you from noticing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is one red grape variety and the wine made from it.

entries.clue: Java product, perhaps filling island cocktail (9)

blocks.note: an applet is a small program, typically written in the Java language

annotation.surface: Coffee from Java goes into a tropical-island cocktail.
annotation.walkthrough: Java suggests the Indonesian island or its coffee; here it is the programming language.
annotation.definitionFit: An appletini is an apple-flavoured martini cocktail.

entries.clue: Relax topless somewhere in Germany (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so drop it

blocks.note: to lessen is to relax, ease off; drop the L

annotation.surface: Sunbathers go topless at a German resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' fits the beach surface; in a down answer it removes the top letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, western Germany.

entries.clue: Broad humour out of reach these days (5)

blocks.note: CE = Common Era, the current era

annotation.surface: Coarse comedy has fallen out of fashion nowadays.
annotation.walkthrough: CE (Common Era) is the neutral label for the present era, used in place of AD.
annotation.definitionFit: Broad means coarse and unsubtle, and the answer is the knockabout stage comedy built on exactly that.

entries.clue: Swear in cricket match? (6)

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match

annotation.surface: A player curses during a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: A Test match is a multi-day international cricket fixture; 'Swear' suggests cursing but means to declare on oath.
annotation.definitionFit: To attest is to swear or declare that something is true.

entries.clue: Teacher training left large blunder in writing (8)

blocks.note: Miss, how pupils address a female teacher
L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A trainee teacher has left a big mistake in a pupil's essay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teacher training' reads as one phrase; it splits into Miss and PE.
annotation.definitionFit: Getting a word's letters wrong is the textbook blunder of writing; the definition simply describes the act.

entries.clue: Tiresome, what judges get up to (6)

definitions.note: 'what judges get up to' is a noun phrase for the activity; trying is the gerund naming it.

blocks.note: judges spend their days hearing cases in court

annotation.surface: A weary remark that the antics of judges are tedious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get up to' suggests mischief; it only means what judges do in court.
annotation.definitionFit: Trying means tiresome, and it is also what judges do to cases.

entries.clue: Trusting pub with old foreign money (8)

blocks.note: a cent is a coin in dollar or euro countries

annotation.surface: A naive traveller takes old foreign coins into a pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trusting' reads as a verb in the surface; the definition is the adjective, naive.
annotation.definitionFit: An innocent person is trusting, lacking guile.
